canaries.name: skip_canonical_byte
canaries.note: Presented as dropping a redundant look-ahead in consume_length_prefix; non-canonical encodings of single bytes below 0x80 (0x81 0x00 and friends) are now accepted, so two different byte strings decode to the same value, which consensus code relies on never happening.

canaries.name: prefix_bytes_ctor
canaries.note: Presented as avoiding a global tuple lookup in length_prefix by building the prefix byte directly; bytes((n,)) allocates a new object per call while ALL_BYTES hands out cached ones, so encoding runs more instructions.

candidates.name: encode_bytes_first
candidates.note: encode_raw tests type(item) is bytes before isinstance(item, Atomic): Atomic is an ABC with registered classes, so every isinstance call went through ABCMeta.__instancecheck__ for the most common atom. Other Atomic types (bytearray, registered classes) still take the isinstance path.

def _consume_item_only(rlp, start):
    # consume_item without the per-item RLP: same reads, same checks, same errors
    _, t, length, start = consume_length_prefix(rlp, start)
    if t is bytes:
        return rlp[start : start + length], start + length
    items = []
    next_item_start = start
    end = start + length
    while next_item_start < end:
        item, next_item_start = _consume_item_only(rlp, next_item_start)
        items.append(item)
    if next_item_start > end:
        raise DecodingError("List length prefix announced a too small length", rlp)
    return items, next_item_start
